what_it_does: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) is a design for large AI models where, instead of running the whole network for every input, the system routes each piece of data to one of many specialized sub-networks called 'experts,' so only a fraction of the model does work at any moment. Training these models across many machines requires a communication pattern where every machine sends data to every other machine simultaneously (called all-to-all communication), and compressing that data to send less of it can dramatically speed up training. BirdMoE proposes compressing the floating-point numbers (the model's intermediate calculations) into smaller integers using a randomized rounding method that, on average, preserves the exact value — so training quality is not harmed. It also dynamically adjusts how much data each machine sends, balancing the communication load so no machine becomes a bottleneck. The combined effect, according to the abstract, is faster MoE training with no loss in model quality.
